Physics Lab

A storm tips 400 crates onto the Reef's harbor. Each fixed physics step pays for awake bodies and for every pair of colliders that touch. Change the colliders, let bodies sleep, and set how many steps a slow frame may catch up.

Harbor in the storm, mid-range phone, 30 fps, fixed step 16.67 ms (2 steps a frame). Goal: physics at most 4 ms a frame, and the game back at 2 steps after a hitch.

Catch-up, frame by frame

Lesson 038: physics cost and how to tame it

    What this shows

    Contacts are the bill

    A pile of 400 crates has about 1,000 touching pairs. Each pair costs collision detection plus solver work, every step, twice a frame.

    Simple shapes, sleeping bodies

    A box is the cheapest test there is, and a mesh floor is one of the most expensive. Bodies that rest and aren't pushed fall asleep and cost almost nothing.

    The spiral of death

    When steps are slow, a hitch makes the next frame run more of them, which makes it slower again. Cap the catch-up, and keep each step cheap enough to recover.

    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses Lesson 038's numbers: the rest of the frame 14 ms; the rest of the harbor's physics 1.0 ms a step; an awake body 2.5 µs; solver 1.2 µs a pair; detection 3.8 µs for two convex meshes, 0.6 µs for two boxes, 8.8 µs for a crate on the 20,000-triangle mesh floor and 0.6 µs on a simple box. The pile: 1,000 crate pairs and 250 crate–floor pairs; with waves only in the water, 60 crates stay awake with 150 and 40 pairs. The catch-up rule: steps = frame time ÷ 16.67 ms, rounded up, at least 2, at most the cap.
